basis:
WHAT THIS FILE IS. The observed ENVELOPE of every entry the speed gate measures — the range it was actually seen over, with a tolerance, and never a single number pretending to be one. Recorded on the cell that reads it: ubuntu-latest, image ubuntu24/20260927.320, runner 2.337.0.

THREE WINDOWS. The renderer workloads ship IDENTICAL code at all three commits; the rounds between them touched the workflow, the tests, the comparator and this document, never a renderer:

    window 1  07:46-07:56Z  at 3c30eca  runs 36832215161 36832519319 36832824918 36833056763
    window 2  10:15-10:24Z  at 4c003c6  runs 36847969226 36848207890 36848474648 36848721383
    window 3  10:35-10:47Z  at 94e8a78  runs 36850024437 36850406095 36850650070 36850880222 36851111411

Every per-window figure below was reproduced to six decimals from the raw `time` and `gh-wall` attributes of those thirteen runs' artifacts, and the envelopes are the union of all 26 round observations in them:

    entry                         window 1        window 2        window 3        union
    counter::unit-suite            16.593-23.203   22.852-24.544   21.657-24.360   21.657-24.544
    e2e::bench.render               0.056- 0.084     0.080- 0.087     0.079- 0.084   0.056- 0.090
    e2e::bench.render-impact        1.019- 1.351     1.332- 1.404     1.045- 1.355   1.019- 1.441
    e2e::bench.render-responsiveness 0.060- 0.080     0.078- 0.086     0.078- 0.082   0.060- 0.087

An earlier revision of this file recorded maxima of 0.090278, 1.414891 and 0.087334 for the three workloads — figures carried forward from a summary table rather than derived from the runs, and two of them exceeded every observation in the artifacts they cited, while the third was attributed to the wrong window. The maxima here are the ones the artifacts actually contain. The error was in the safe direction — every recorded maximum clears every per-run minimum, so no run the cell has shown can false-red — but "the union of the runs" is a claim about the runs, and it was not one.

THE SPREAD IS NOT A PROPERTY OF THE WORKLOAD. It is the workload AND the state of the pool during the window: window 1 contains one clearly fast machine and several slow ones, windows 2 and 3 look like a quiet pool. That is why the envelopes are unions and not the last window's figures. DO NOT SHRINK A TOLERANCE BECAUSE THE LAST RUNS WERE QUIET, and do not read a quiet window as the cell's characteristic spread.

WHY THE TOLERANCES ARE WHAT THEY ARE — A STRUCTURAL ARGUMENT, NOT AN EMPIRICAL ONE. This gate compares a per-run MINIMUM against a recorded MAXIMUM. Its false-red risk comes from the head landing HIGH — above the recorded maximum. The spread of the recorded window, folded in as a single fraction, covers the LOW tail too, which this gate cannot be hurt by. So the rule is conservative by construction: it measures in one direction and protects in the other. That is the correct side to err on for a gate whose failure mode is a red on main that teaches people to ignore it, and it is the reason the tolerances are the observed spreads rather than something tighter.

What the data does NOT support is the claim this file previously made, that a tolerance of 0.40 was needed to stop the suite false-reding on a busy run. Window 1's 39.8% for the suite is a LOW-tail artefact — one run at 16.6 against a body of 22.2-23.2 — so it is evidence of one fast machine, not of a busy pool, and a tolerance near the quiet-window spread would not have false-reded. That claim is withdrawn. The conservative tolerance stays anyway, for the structural reason above and not for the empirical one.

THE UNIT SUITE'S ENVELOPE SPANS TWO WINDOWS, ITS TOLERANCE DOES NOT SHRINK. Windows 2 and 3 ran a tree whose suite matches this one's; window 1's suite was a shorter, different population and is excluded on that ground rather than on its spread. The envelope takes both windows' extremes (21.657-24.544). The tolerance is 0.40: this gate compares a per-run minimum against a recorded maximum, so the high tail is what can red it, and the fraction is the one measurement the cell offers in the same direction. 0.40 is wider than the 13.3% either window showed, and that width is the conservatism described above.

WHAT THIS GATE THEREFORE CATCHES, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. The honest summary is uncomfortable. At these tolerances a DOUBLED workload is caught on the unit suite and on NONE of the three renderer workloads: doubling the fastest machine observed lands under all three ceilings. Tightening any of them to catch its doubling means going below its own observed spread — a ceiling the fastest machine already clears, which would fire on ordinary pool variation. A gate that cries wolf is deader than one with a documented blind spot, so bench.render is NOT tuned and neither are its siblings. The gate catches a gross step change and the gross wall smoke bound; it will not catch a 20% regression anywhere. Read "load-invariant counter" as "a quantity the machine's load does not reach", not as "a sharp budget".

THE GROSS WALL SMOKE BOUND. `wall` is an envelope for the same reason, spanning the same three windows; at SMOKE_FACTOR 3.0 the ceilings are 168.6 seconds, 0.261, 4.69 and 0.261. `test_baseline.py` recomputes all four from this document, because a transcribed ceiling was wrong twice in this file's history. That bound is deliberately not a budget: it is a cliff detector for the class CPU cannot see at all, a workload getting slower in wall while its CPU cost holds flat, which is what blocking on I/O, a network call or a lock wait looks like. The report prints no elapsed time at all: a verdict and no number.

PROVENANCE, AND THE ONE PLACE THE DIGEST AND THE ENVELOPES ARE NOT FROM THE SAME TREE. measured_commit is 94e8a78, the remote head the five dispatches resolved --ref issue-81-82 against, and every envelope above was observed there. `population` is the digest of the node ids THIS tree collects, computed by running collect_node_ids over it rather than copied from anywhere — which is what the guard compares, and re-deriving it here is what keeps that guard meaningful rather than silenced.

That leaves one honest gap, stated rather than hidden: this tree collects more node ids than 94e8a78 did, because the commits since added the controls that govern this very document. The RENDERER envelopes are unaffected — WORKLOADS did not change and no renderer did, so their union describes this tree exactly. The UNIT envelope is an estimate for it: more collected tests is more work, and the next dispatch of this head re-derives it from runs of the program this tree actually runs. Until then the unit figure is the best available record and is labelled as such.

A NOTE ON THE UNIT SUITE'S SOURCE RUNS. Window 3's five dispatches exited non-zero: the suite's own population-digest control was red, because at that commit the baseline still described an older tree. The counters were recorded regardless. The work the control was asserting about is a document check, not a change in what the suite does, so the measurements stand — but a dispatch whose suite is green is the cleaner source, and this file says so rather than presenting five red runs as though nothing had happened.

HOW TO RE-DERIVE. Run the job four or five times on the cell that will read it, and take each entry's min and max ACROSS dispatches AND across windows rather than within one — a single quiet window is not a measurement of the cell, it is a measurement of a quiet afternoon. Keep every window's figures: the widest one seen for an entry governs. Re-derive, never carry, and never shrink because the latest runs were kind.
